text: Application Insights isn't a separate product — it's Azure Monitor's lens aimed at one running application: what requests came in, how long each took, what that request called out to, and what broke along the way. All of that lands in the same kind of Log Analytics-backed workspace from last lesson, in its own set of tables, queryable with the exact same KQL you already know.

Telemetry gets collected one of two ways. SDK-based instrumentation adds a package and a connection string to the application's code, giving the richest detail, including custom events you add yourself. Codeless monitoring attaches an agent at the platform level instead — no code changes, capturing the same core signals: requests, dependencies, and exceptions. Either way, the data ends up in the same queryable tables.

Four tables carry most of the weight: requests for every inbound call, dependencies for every outbound call the application made, exceptions for unhandled errors with their stack traces, and traces for whatever the application logged explicitly. This query finds the slowest endpoint right now — the same summarize and order-by shape from last lesson's Perf query, just pointed at application data instead of infrastructure counters.

Every row Application Insights writes for one logical request — the inbound requests row and every dependencies row it triggered — shares the same operation_Id. That shared field is what turns scattered rows into one connected story: filter every table to one operation_Id, and you've reconstructed the exact call chain for one specific slow or failed request, the same way a trace walked through a dominant span back in Lesson 1, except now it's real application data.

Two features build on this without writing a single query. Live Metrics streams requests, dependencies, and exceptions with sub-second latency, useful for watching a deployment roll out live. The Application Map draws every component the application talks to as a diagram, with failure rates and durations on each connection, so you can spot a dragging downstream service visually. Next lesson moves to Container Insights — the same kind of tracing, now for workloads running on AKS.
